title: Selling Home Franklin TN Fall Mistakes: 7 to Avoid
description: Seven costly mistakes when selling a home in Franklin, TN this fall, from stale comps and overpricing to weak photos, with current local market data.
keyword: selling home Franklin TN fall mistakes
body:
Most sellers who struggle in the fall did not have a bad house. They made a few avoidable decisions early, and those decisions were hard to undo once the listing sat. Here are seven mistakes I see sellers make, and what to do instead.

First, a look at the local numbers, because they shape everything below. In Franklin, the median sale price was $863,000, up 12.8% from a year earlier, with a median of 49 days on market and an average sale-to-list ratio of 98.3% (Redfin, rolling 3 months, data as of 2026-08-31). Those are citywide figures. Your home, price range and street can look different.

## Pricing mistakes: old comps and ignored competition

{{img:0}}

**Mistake one: pricing from old comps.** A sale from six months ago tells you what a buyer paid then. It does not tell you what a buyer will pay this month. Zillow Research shows Franklin's Market Temperature Index at 46, down 6 points over three months, which points to a cooling trend (Zillow Research, as of 2026-08-31). Pricing from a spring sale can leave you above where buyers are now.

Start with the most recent closed sales of similar homes, and give the newest ones the most weight. Your agent can pull these from [RealTracs MLS](https://www.realtracs.com). You can also check public records yourself on the [Williamson County property search](https://www.williamsoncounty-tn.gov/2099/35739/Property-Data-Search).

The pricing question is rarely about what you need to net. It is about what the market is paying for a home like yours right now. If you want a starting point, the [home value page](/sell#form) is a good place to begin.

**Mistake two: ignoring active listings and price cuts.** Closed sales show the past. Active listings show your real competition. Redfin reports 531 active listings in Franklin and 3.4 months of supply (Redfin, rolling 3 months, as of 2026-08-31). Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 is balanced, and over 6 favors buyers.

A citywide number does not mean your price range moves at the same pace. Look at what is listed near you, how long those homes have sat, and which ones have dropped their price. A listing that has been cut twice is telling you something about where buyers drew the line. The [Franklin housing market data](/franklin/housing-market) page is one place to track the broader picture.

## Presentation mistakes: curb appeal, renovations and photos

**Mistake three: skipping curb appeal.** Buyers form an opinion before they reach the door. Fall brings leaves, dull beds and fading paint on trim. Raking, pressure washing, fresh mulch, a clean front door and working exterior lights cost little compared with a price reduction. Simple, tidy and well lit is the goal.

**Mistake four: over-renovating before you list.** A big kitchen or bath project right before listing can eat your net proceeds, and there is no guarantee you will get that money back in the sale price. Repairs buyers will notice anyway, such as a stained ceiling, a broken fixture or peeling paint, are usually the better use of money. Before you spend on anything large, ask your agent how similar homes in your price range have sold with and without that upgrade.

**Mistake five: weak photos.** Most buyers see your home online first. Dark rooms, cluttered counters, a car in the driveway and photos taken at dusk make a home look smaller and less cared for. Clear the surfaces, turn on every light, and shoot in daylight. Fall days get shorter, so schedule photos earlier in the day. Also make sure the listing has complete details, including accurate square footage and room counts.

## Offer mistakes: looking only at the price

{{img:1}}

**Mistake six: rejecting an offer without weighing the full terms.** The price is only one line. An offer also includes:

- the financing type, such as conventional, FHA or VA
- the earnest money amount
- the closing date
- inspection and repair requests
- any request for the seller to pay closing costs or fund a rate buydown

Buyers can ask for help with closing costs or a buydown, and whether that works depends on the seller, the home, the market and what the buyer's lender allows. For context, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.40% (Freddie Mac via FRED, week of 2026-10-08). You can see the current figure on the Freddie Mac rate page. When rates are at that level, some buyers will ask for help with costs.

A slightly lower price with a clean, quick close can leave you in a different spot than a higher price with a long list of contingencies. Compare offers by what you would actually walk away with and how likely each is to reach closing. Your agent can help you lay them side by side. For tax questions, talk with a tax professional.

Also expect the usual requests. Termite and wood-destroying organism inspections are commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee, and the residential property condition disclosure (or exemption) is part of the sale. If your home was built before 1978, the lead-based paint disclosure applies. The [Tennessee Real Estate Commission](https://www.tn.gov/commerce/regboards/trec.html) has official information on these rules.

## Planning mistake: no plan if early interest is slow

**Mistake seven: having no plan for a slow start.** Most sellers plan for the offers they want and not for silence. The first stretch after listing usually brings the most attention, so if showings are light, do not just wait.

Decide before you list when you will review. At that point, sit down with your agent and look at:

- showing counts and any feedback
- how your photos and description compare to nearby listings
- new competing listings and recent price changes
- whether the price still fits the latest closed sales

Nashville metro numbers give a wider view. Redfin shows 5.4 months of supply and a median of 68 days on market for the four weeks ending 2026-09-27, with a sale-to-list ratio of 97.8% (Redfin, Nashville metro). That is a more balanced picture than Franklin's 3.4 months, which is a reminder that conditions differ by area and price range. See the [Redfin Data Center](https://www.redfin.com/news/data-center/) for current figures. Realtor.com Research also puts Williamson County hotness at 41.7 of 100 (Realtor.com Research, as of the latest data supplied), another sign that attention is not what it was.

None of this predicts what your listing will do. It is a reason to have a plan rather than a hope.

## Next steps

If you are thinking about selling in Franklin this fall, start with an honest look at pricing, presentation and a review plan. You can read more on [selling a home in Franklin](/franklin/selling-in-franklin), or use the seller form to ask about your home's value. If you would rather talk it through first, [contact Scott](/contact) directly.

faq.q: How do I avoid overpricing my home in Franklin, TN?
faq.a: Base your price on the most recent closed sales of similar homes and on what is currently listed near you, not on older sales. Franklin's Zillow Market Temperature Index was 46, down 6 points over three months (Zillow Research, as of 2026-08-31).

faq.q: How long do homes take to sell in Franklin right now?
faq.a: Redfin reports a median of 49 days on market in Franklin (rolling 3 months, data as of 2026-08-31). Your home may sell faster or slower depending on its price, condition and location.

Large projects can cost more than they return, and there is no guarantee. Ask your agent how similar homes in your price range have sold before spending on big upgrades, and consider fixing the small things buyers will notice.

faq.q: Should I turn down an offer that is below my asking price?
faq.a: Compare the full terms first, including financing type, closing date, inspection requests and any closing cost or rate buydown request. The highest price is not always the strongest offer.

issues: Article 12 / unsupported claim: "Most sellers who struggle in the fall did not have a bad house. They made a few avoidable decisions early, and those decisions were hard to undo once the listing sat." This is a sweeping generalization about 'most sellers' with no supplied data or source.
Article 12 / unverifiable generalization: "Most buyers see your home online first." This reads as a statistic and has no source or date in the supplied facts.
Article 12 / unverifiable generalization: "The first stretch after listing usually brings the most attention." This market-behavior claim is not in the supplied facts and is stated as fact.

Missing or invented date for a statistic: "Zillow Research shows Franklin's Market Temperature Index at 46, down 6 points over three months ... (Zillow Research, as of 2026-08-31)." The facts supply no as-of date for the Zillow figure. The 2026-08-31 date belongs to the Redfin data. The same unsupported date is repeated in the FAQ: "Franklin's Zillow Market Temperature Index was 46, down 6 points over three months (Zillow Research, as of 2026-08-31)."

Missing source date / unsupported inference: "Realtor.com Research also puts Williamson County hotness at 41.7 of 100 (Realtor.com Research, as of the latest data supplied), another sign that attention is not what it was." 'As of the latest data supplied' is not a real date. The facts give no prior reading, so 'not what it was' is an unsupported trend claim. Hotness is also a county figure, not a Franklin one.

Unsupported legal/program claim: "The Tennessee Real Estate Commission has official information on these rules." The supplied facts do not say TREC is the source for the disclosure or WDO rules, and the lead-based paint rule is federal.
Article 12 / speculation stated as fact: "When rates are at that level, some buyers will ask for help with costs." This predicts buyer behavior and is not supported by the supplied facts.
